title: otel/ adapter: kbmon's metric points over OTLP/HTTP with the SDK, pinned by its own uv.lock, off until an endpoint is set
goal: otel/kbmon_otel.py run as uv run --frozen --project otel python otel/kbmon_otel.py sends kbmon's metric points to /v1/metrics over OTLP/HTTP with the OpenTelemetry Python SDK, pinned in otel/uv.lock, taking the endpoint and headers from the SDK's standard OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS; it never prints or logs a header value; with no endpoint set it sends nothing and says export is off; _tools/ imports no OpenTelemetry package

notes: Plan 2026-10-18 (operator interview): the operator chose a separate SDK adapter over a stdlib OTLP encoder, in a top-level otel/ with its own pyproject.toml and uv.lock, run by uv --frozen, the checks allowed to fill uv's cache once. The checks are python3 scripts that run the adapter through uv and receive on a stdlib http.server; protobuf strings are raw bytes, so names and planted secrets are found in the body without decoding. kb: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is a base URL to which v1/<signal> is appended (claude/otel-monitoring.md:38, DOC S-kumwk4fp); OTLP/HTTP posts to /v1/metrics, /v1/logs, /v1/traces on port 4318 (logs/otel-collector-otlp-pipeline.md:35, DOC S-v2wnj4qk).
